23:- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
47:- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
62:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7 → v8 → v9 → v10 → v11 → v12 → v13 → v14 → v15 → v16.
`effectPoisonTimer`) are likewise transient — but the effects **themselves**
(`state.effects`) persist via the `effects` field above and survive a reload.

### Version history

- **v16** (water vehicles) — adds optional top-level `vehicles` (`SavedVehicle[]`) for placed **rafts** and **ships**. `migrateSaveV15toV16` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no placed vehicles). Vehicle items are additive string ids; placed vehicles are entities, not voxel blocks, so there is **no `BlockId` or worldgen change** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 9). The rider/mount state is transient and reloads with the player unmounted.
- **v15** (villager professions — Living World, PR 2) — adds an optional `profession` (`"farmer" | "blacksmith" | "librarian" | "cleric"`) on a villager resident's `SavedMob`. `migrateSaveV14toV15` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ the engine assigns one round-robin at boot). Validated against the known professions on load. **Generated villages** in the same release bump **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 8→9** (villages add structures, so old block-diffs are stale and discarded — the worldgen/world-type/meshing digests were re-baselined per docs/testing.md); village residents persist via the existing v14 `mobs` field, and **raids** are transient (`state.raid` + raiders aren't serialized, like the boss), so neither needs further save schema beyond the additive `profession` and the by-id Ominous Horn item.
- **v14** (persisted mobs — Living World, PR 1) — adds an optional top-level `mobs` (`SavedMob[]`). `migrateSaveV13toV14` is a pure version bump (absent ⇒ no persisted mobs; the world re-seeds its wildlife as before). This is the first mob persistence in the format: `isPersistentMob` keeps only **tamed pets** here (PR-B adds village residents), since the fungible population is re-created each boot. Restored before `spawnInitialMobs`, with `y` re-grounded onto the current surface and fresh ids assigned. The wolf and cat are additive `MobKind`s with no `BlockId`/item changes, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.

No new `BlockId`, no new item, and no worldgen change — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.
- **Unreleased (no save bump)** — new enchantments (**Power**, **Punch**, **Knockback**, **Looting**, **Fortune**, **Feather Falling**) ride the existing per-slot `enchantments` field, and new status effects (**Haste**, **Resistance**, **Jump Boost**) ride the existing top-level `effects` field. Their ids are added to the save validators' known-id sets (`VALID_ENCHANT_IDS` / `VALID_EFFECT_IDS`, both compile-enforced `Record<…, true>`). No new field, no new `BlockId`, no worldgen change — the save schema stays **v12** and **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** (the same additive-id pattern as Mending). Older builds silently drop unknown ids on load.
- **v12** (dedicated armor storage) — fixes a bug where equipped armor stayed in the inventory and occupied a hotbar/storage slot. `equippedArmor` is no longer a by-id reference into `inventorySlots` but the worn pieces themselves, persisted per slot as `SavedSlot` (via `serializeEquippedArmor`/`restoreEquippedArmor`, reusing the shared `restoreSlot` validation). `migrateSaveV11toV12` moves each legacy by-id equip out of `inventorySlots` into the armor record (preserving durability/enchantments/customName; equips whose item isn't found or isn't valid armor are dropped; a legacy `inventoryCounts`-only save just drops the equip map and keeps the items). No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and `SAVE_KEY` is unchanged.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **The aquatic update**: the ocean the new rafts and ships sail is now worth sailing — fish, flora, wrecks to dive, and treasure to hunt, all on **zero binary assets**. Bumps **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10** (kelp/coral/wrecks/buried chests write generated blocks, so existing worlds reboot from their seed and every worldgen/world-type/meshing digest except flat was re-baselined per docs/testing.md) with **no save-schema change** — the schema stays **v16**.
  - **Kelp & coral**: the sandy ocean floor grows swaying **kelp stalks** and pink/blue **reef coral** (a new hash-gated `placeOceanFlora` pass that consumes no shared PRNG). Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (the wheat trick — no new geometry): stalks always keep a **3-block clear-water band** below the surface so boats and fishing casts never snag, growth via the existing random-tick sampler enforces the same cap, and **breaking a cell breaks the stalk above it, refilling submerged cells with water — never air**. Kelp smelts **3-at-a-time into dried kelp** (a 2-hunger snack); corals are decorative salvage. New `BlockId`s **appended** (55–57)
  - **Cod & salmon**: the first water-dwelling mobs. A dedicated **aquatic AI branch** (3D wander/flee, every move gated on the destination cell being water, no ground clamp) runs before any land logic; a beached fish flops and suffocates. Both drop **raw fish** — the recipe-book hint for it now reads "Hunt a cod". Fish are fungible (never persisted; old saves load cleanly), spawn as schools in whatever water lies near spawn, and a new **aquatic spawn director** trickles them in around the player (up to `AQUATIC_CAP` 24) so far-flung oceans are stocked too — failing closed on dry worlds (Superflat spawns none). Legless "fish" model variant on `createMobModel`, bubble-blip ZZFX calls
  - **Shipwrecks**: flooded plank hulls (broken walls, snapped mast, always fully submerged) sink onto the deep ocean floor on their own decoupled PRNG, holding 1–2 chests of nautical salvage — and the **treasure map** at a 40% roll. The dungeon lazy-fill generalizes to `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`: the site set holding a chest's index picks both the loot table and a family-distinct seed constant, and **all families share the persisted `lootedChests` field unchanged** (no re-roll exploit, no save bump)
  - **Buried treasure & the treasure map**: hold a map (wreck loot, or a rare fishing catch) and a **compass pill** points at the *nearest* unearthed hoard while red **X**s mark the minimap; dig two blocks under the beach sand for the richest chest table in the game (emeralds guaranteed). The map is deliberately **stateless** — no per-item target, no save field: the compass derives everything from the seed and retargets automatically after each dig. Chests place on a fourth decoupled PRNG with a **seed-pure beach proxy** (terrain-height band + a below-sea neighbor column — never post-water block reads), sand-capped so a breaching cave can't expose them. First dig fires the new **treasureUnearthed** event → **X Marks the Spot** advancement + a **Treasures Unearthed** statistic
- **Rafts and ships**: craftable water vehicles on **zero binary assets**.

Done — the aquatic update is fully built. Here's the summary:

## What I recommended and built

You asked for next-feature recommendations. My top pick was an **aquatic update** (the ocean your new rafts and ships sail was empty — nothing to see, nothing to sail to), with runner-ups being a deferred-mechanics batch, a Nether-style dimension, and redstone-lite. The plan question timed out, so I proceeded with the recommended option after you approved the plan.

It's complete on the local branch `feat/aquatic-update` — **5 commits, not pushed** (per your review-first workflow):

1. **Kelp & coral** — swaying kelp stalks and pink/blue reef coral on the sandy ocean floor. Kelp keeps a 3-block clear-water band so boats never snag, regrows via random ticks, harvests as a full stalk (refilling with water, never air pockets), and smelts 3-at-a-time into dried kelp.
2. **Cod & salmon** — the first water-dwelling mobs, with a dedicated 3D swim/flee AI branch that can never leave water, a legless fish model variant, and an aquatic spawn director so oceans you sail to are stocked (zero fish on Superflat — the sampler fails closed).
3. **Shipwrecks** — flooded plank hulls sunk on the deep ocean floor with 1–2 loot chests of nautical salvage. The dungeon lazy-fill system generalized to per-family loot tables and seed constants.
4. **Buried treasure & the treasure map** — loot a map from a wreck (40%) or fish one up, follow a compass HUD to the beach, dig two blocks under the sand for the richest chest in the game. The map is stateless (compass derives from the seed, retargets after each dig), plus minimap X marks and an "X Marks the Spot" advancement.
5. **Docs** — manual, reference, tuning, adding-content, testing, save-format, CHANGELOG, and README all updated (including two stale version numbers I found in tuning.md).

## Impact & verification

- **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10** (old worlds reboot from their seed, digests re-baselined per policy); **save schema stays v16** — no migration needed.
- Full gate green at every commit: lint, typecheck, format, **984 unit tests** (35 new), build, and **18/18 Playwright e2e**.

## What's left for you

- **A manual gameplay pass** on an ocean seed (kelp/coral/fish visuals, wreck diving, compass feel, bubble SFX) — the wolf/cat spawn bug taught us not to skip this before a release.
- Review the 5 commits, then tell me to push / open the PR when you're happy.

Explicitly deferred: a drowned-like hostile (fish AI doesn't give it pursuit or underwater LOS cheaply), full cartographic map rendering, and fish buckets/breeding.

## Summary

The ocean the new rafts and ships sail is now worth sailing: living fish, ocean-floor flora, sunken wrecks to dive, and a treasure hunt to follow. All on **zero binary assets**, in five reviewable slices (one commit each).

- **Kelp & coral** — swaying kelp stalks and pink/blue reef coral generate on the sandy ocean floor (a new hash-gated `placeOceanFlora` pass that consumes no shared PRNG). Kelp is a solid cube painted to read as a plant (the wheat trick): stalks always keep a 3-block clear-water band below the surface so boats and casts never snag, growth via the existing random-tick sampler enforces the same cap, and breaking a cell breaks the stalk above it, **refilling submerged cells with water — never air**. Kelp smelts 3-at-a-time into dried kelp (a 2-hunger snack). New `BlockId`s appended (55–57).
- **Cod & salmon** — the first water-dwelling mobs. A dedicated aquatic AI branch runs before any land logic: 3D wander/flee with every move gated on the destination cell being water (no ground clamp), and a beached fish flops and suffocates. Fish are fungible (never persisted; old saves load cleanly); a new aquatic spawn director trickles schools in around the player up to `AQUATIC_CAP`, failing closed on dry worlds — Superflat spawns none. Legless "fish" variant on `createMobModel`; both drop raw fish (the recipe-book hint now reads "Hunt a cod").
- **Shipwrecks** — flooded plank hulls (broken walls, snapped mast, always fully submerged) sink onto the deep ocean floor on their own decoupled PRNG, holding 1–2 chests of nautical salvage and the **treasure map** at a 40% roll. The dungeon lazy-fill generalizes to `fillWorldgenChestIfUnlooted`: the site set holding a chest's index picks both the loot table and a family-distinct seed constant, and all families share the persisted `lootedChests` field unchanged (no re-roll exploit, no save bump).
- **Buried treasure & the treasure map** — hold a map and a compass pill points at the *nearest* unearthed hoard while red Xs mark the minimap; dig two blocks under the beach sand for the richest chest table in the game (emeralds guaranteed). The map is deliberately **stateless** — no per-item target, no save field: the compass derives everything from the seed and retargets automatically after each dig. Chests place on a fourth decoupled PRNG with a seed-pure beach proxy (terrain-height band + a below-sea neighbor column — never post-water block reads), sand-capped so a breaching cave can't expose them. First dig fires `treasureUnearthed` → the **X Marks the Spot** advancement and a **Treasures Unearthed** statistic.
- **Docs** — manual ("The ocean"), reference tables + loot tables, tuning (incl. two stale version numbers fixed), adding-content seams (generalized worldgen-chest fill; aquatic-mob template flag), testing coverage map, save-format entry, CHANGELOG, README blurb.

## Save & worldgen impact

- **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` 9→10** (bumped once): kelp/coral/wrecks/buried chests write generated blocks, so existing worlds discard stale block-diffs and reboot from their seed. Every worldgen/world-type/meshing digest except flat was re-baselined per docs/testing.md, with structural probes for each new feature.
- **Save schema stays v16** — no migration: fish are never persisted, kelp rides the block diff, the new items are stateless string ids, and worldgen chests reuse the persisted `lootedChests` set (state-side renamed `lootedWorldgenChests`; the save field name is unchanged, so pre-aquatic saves read as-is).

## Deferred (follow-up candidates)

A drowned-like hostile (needs 3D water pursuit, a water-aware hostile spawn director, and underwater LOS — not cheap on top of fish AI), full cartographic map rendering, and fish buckets/breeding.

## Testing

- Full gate green at every commit: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test` (**984 tests**, 35 new), `bun run build`, and `bun run test:e2e` (**18/18**).
- New coverage: ocean-flora/shipwreck/buried-treasure worldgen probes (every generated chest belongs to a known site; derives are deterministic), kelp growth caps + cascade-break refill, fish water-confinement/3D flee/beach suffocation, fail-closed aquatic spawning, per-family chest fill + the retargeting compass, and loot-table integrity for both new tables.
- **A manual gameplay pass on an ocean seed is still recommended before merging** (kelp/coral/fish visuals, wreck diving, compass/minimap feel, bubble SFX) — the new visuals aren't headless-verifiable.
